html:
Féénemɨnaa appears to be the self-name of the Muinane, a small people of the Colombian Amazon between the Caquetá and Putumayo rivers. They speak a language of the Bora family, distinct from the Witoto of the Murui-Muinane nearby.

Little is recorded of them before 1900. Like their neighbours they were forced into rubber collecting in the Putumayo atrocities of the rubber boom, and their numbers fell sharply. They live today in reserves in Colombia.
